content_note: Every rule here is intent-only: a name, an id and a logic line that names the detections the rule would join. There is no query, schedule, severity or alert mapping, so nothing in this file can be imported into a tenant as-is. Author the rule in the XSIAM console from the logic line.

rules.logic: Fires when analytics `Azure conditional access policy creation or modification` (or abioc `Conditional-access policy weakened off the learned admin-change baseline`) on msft_azure_audit and analytics `Azure mailbox rule creation` (or abioc `External mailbox forwarding rule off the learned inbox-rule baseline`) on msft_o365_audit both fire within a 30-minute persistence window. The two legs land in different datasets with different identity fields (the CA record carries identity.claims.appid; the inbox-rule record carries UserId), so the rule stitches on temporal co-occurrence within the campaign window rather than a single shared identity-field value, raising one two-stage Azure identity-persistence incident: the actor first relaxes conditional-access enforcement, then plants a covert external mail-forwarding rule for collection.
rules.name: Azure Identity Persistence — CA policy weakening then covert mail rule
